name: Arcturus Defense Solutions VVR-5 'Dial'
description:
The Arcturus VVR-5 is a variable-voltage shock rod built to military specification, occupying a deliberate space between non-lethal compliance tools and genuinely dangerous weapons. It is a 65-centimeter hardened-polymer baton with a recessed rotary selector on the grip that moves through five discrete output settings: 10,000V (deterrent), 30,000V (compliance), 60,000V (incapacitation), 120,000V (severe incapacitation), and a fifth position marked with a red band and no printed label that delivers 250,000 volts at an amperage approaching the cardiac-disruption threshold. The selector requires a deliberate two-finger press-and-turn action to move between positions, intended to prevent accidental escalation. The VVR-5's power cell is a military-grade capacitor block, field-replaceable in approximately fifteen seconds, with each block providing 30 discharges at maximum setting or 200 at the lowest.

Arcturus developed the VVR-5 in response to contractor feedback from Tier 1 enforcement operations, where the threat environment ranges from unarmed and frightened civilians to heavily augmented territorial enforcers within the same operational area. A single fixed-output weapon requires operators to choose between undertooling for the latter or overtooling for the former. The VVR-5 resolves this by putting that decision at the operator's thumb. Arcturus documentation consistently refers to all five settings as 'less-lethal' while acknowledging in technical footnotes that Setting 5 'may induce cardiac events in subjects with pre-existing cardiovascular conditions or implanted cardiac devices.'

The VVR-5 is issued to Arcturus-contracted enforcement units operating in hostile-environment designations and is not commercially available through standard channels. Several units have entered the secondary market through theft, black-market diversion, and the personal retention of departing contractors, which Arcturus tracks with visible displeasure.
legality: Restricted — Arcturus contractor and military issue only; civilian possession without authorization is a Class 2 weapons violation
specifications:
Length: 650mm
Weight: 940g
Output Settings: 10,000V / 30,000V / 60,000V / 120,000V / 250,000V
Setting 5 Amperage: 0.009A (cardiac threshold range)
Power Cell: Arcturus MilSpec Cap-Block CB-7 (field replaceable)
Discharges per Cell: 200 (S1) / 30 (S5)
Cell Replacement Time: ~15 seconds
Selector: Press-and-turn rotary, two-finger actuation required
Body: MilSpec hardened polymer composite
Price: Φ3,200 (contractor procurement) / Φ5,500–8,000 (secondary market)
tactical_use: VVR-5 operators are trained to begin at Setting 2 for initial contact with unaugmented subjects and escalate only with specific justification. Setting 3 is considered the standard for augmented resistance; Setting 4 for subjects demonstrating active combat augmentation under power. Setting 5 exists in doctrine as an extreme measure for situations where lethal force would otherwise be authorized and a less-lethal outcome is still preferred. In practice, contractor units in Tier 1 operations have been documented using Setting 4 and 5 routinely against minimally augmented subjects, a pattern that has generated ongoing internal and external review.
cultural_context: The VVR-5 is known on the street as 'the dial' or 'the judge,' and its reputation is built almost entirely around Setting 5. In Tier 1 communities with Arcturus enforcement presence, 'getting full-sent' is the phrase for being hit at maximum output — it has the weight of a serious threat in local vernacular, somewhere between 'beaten badly' and 'nearly killed.' The weapon's presence in civilian hands is always treated as a serious indicator of either stolen military hardware or very well-funded criminal organization.
known_users: high-end private security with Arcturus sourcing
organized criminal groups with military hardware access
story_hooks: An Arcturus VVR-5 recovered from a crime scene has a serial number that traces to a unit reported destroyed in a Tier 1 operation two years ago — but the power cell inside it is a manufacturing batch dated three months ago. Someone inside Arcturus logistics is running a diversion pipeline, and the weapons are being sold to someone who knows how to use them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A purposeful baton with a subtle high-tech edge—rigid, authoritative stance. The hardened polymer body tapers slightly toward a reinforced striking end, while the grip section flares minutely to accommodate the recessed rotary selector. No aggressive angles; this is engineered restraint wearing the language of control.
physical_description.dimensions: 650mm overall length; grip section 120mm; striking head 80mm diameter; 45mm diameter rotary selector housing
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial without being cumbersome—940g distributed along the shaft creates deliberate momentum. Feels planted in a closed grip, engineered for sustained holding without fatigue across extended enforcement operations.
physical_description.primary_material: Military-specification hardened polymer composite; core structure likely carbon-reinforced polymer with impact-absorbing elastomer lamination
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical finish with subtle texture grip—non-reflective to minimize target awareness in low-light operations. Selective brushed-metal accents around the selector housing and power-cell access panel. Evidence of use: minor scuff marks consistent with field deployment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey body with darker charcoal grip panels. The rotary selector features discrete voltage-setting markings in faded white text (10K, 30K, 60K, 120K) with the fifth position marked by a single red band and no label—intentional ambiguity.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with shallow crosshatch texture for wet-glove traction. The selector itself has a knurled surface requiring deliberate two-finger manipulation—tactile feedback prevents accidental escalation.
distinctive_features: Recessed rotary selector requiring coordinated press-and-turn action
Red band marking on fifth selector position (unmarked/unlabeled setting)
Visible capacitor-block access panel on lower grip (quick-swap design)
Faint Arcturus Defense Solutions and 'VVR-5' designation stamped into upper body
Faintly luminescent contact points at striking head (residual capacitor field indicators)
Subtle wear pattern on selector knurling—evidence of repeated operator use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (stylized 'A' with targeting reticle) stamped on grip panel; 'VVR-5 DIAL' designation below; contract-issued variants include military procurement codes laser-etched on the capacitor access panel. Secondary-market units often have these markings deliberately obscured.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and serviceable. Well-cared-for contractor weapons show minimal damage; black-market examples exhibit wear consistent with multiple handovers—selector roughness, minor polymer stress cracks near impact points, sometimes poorly applied grip tape over original coating.
